```shiploop-state
{
  "evidence_refs": ["Original request, S1–S2", "Exercise instructions"],
  "headline": "Intake established the requested CLI outcomes, boundaries, and discovery defaults.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "summary": "S1 — Fact: Deliver a Python command-line tool in the repository that reads sales-record CSV files and prints total revenue, revenue by region, and units by product to the invoking terminal; the named repository is the authorized delivery target. Assumption: Accept one or more CSV paths per invocation and process them together. Discovery must first inspect the available workspace and any supplied sample records or documentation to establish column names, revenue calculation, numeric precision, output format, and handling of invalid or missing data; these decisions block implementation and reliable interpretation of the totals. If evidence does not resolve them, record defaults of region, product, quantity, and unit_price columns; revenue as quantity multiplied by unit_price; decimal arithmetic; a readable text summary; and an error for invalid required data. These defaults rule out automatic schema inference and silently skipped records. Fact: This is a command-line entry point, with results visible on invocation; no deployed target is named. Assumption: The invoking local user is the actor, identified by the operating system; each invocation is noninteractive and independent, retains no shared application state across people, devices, or sessions, and ends when the process exits. File and terminal access controls determine what others can see. Discovery must first establish the available Python runtime and any existing CLI or storage conventions; this blocks runtime compatibility and could change those defaults. Discovery source hints, not verified facts: the workspace, sample CSVs, project documentation, relevant owners or team channels, internal sites, and private repositories if available; none is named in the request. Keep sensitive locators only in an authorized private store, never in committed KNOWLEDGE/. Risks include ambiguous sales schemas, currency or rounding assumptions, and malformed records. Fact: This intake implements nothing; the isolated checkout stays at its snapshot until final return, and the tool becomes usable in the delivered checkout after implementation and return. S2 — Fact: Add tests for the requested calculations and command-line behavior, visible in the delivered repository and when the test suite runs. Discovery must first establish the available test runner and project conventions; this blocks the test setup. If no convention exists, the recorded default is Python's standard-library unittest."
}
```
